title: SBI client never recovers from a half-dead HTTP/2 connection (requests keep timing out forever)

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

body:
After a short request-rate overload, one NF (observed: AMF sending to SMF) can end up talking to a
peer connection that is silently dead: **TCP stays ESTABLISHED, both socket queues are empty, the
peer's event loop is idle (and it answers brand-new connections in sub-millisecond time), but the
peer's application never answers anything on the established connection again.**

Because the SBI client is built on libcurl multi with HTTP/2 multiplexing, aborting an individual
transfer (which is what `connection_timer_expired()` does via `curl_multi_remove_handle()`) does
**not** close the multiplexed connection. libcurl therefore keeps reusing the same dead connection
for every subsequent request, and every request times out until the process is restarted.

Measured on our rig (single AMF, 20 000 UEs registering at ~500/s, deadline 3 s):

- AMF→SMF request timeouts: **23 815** messages in one overload window (all
  `Connection timer expired … POST …/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts`).
- tcpdump on that connection: AMF sent 65 353 data segments; the SMF only ACKed at TCP level and
  sent **no application bytes for 255 s**.
- `ss -K dst <smf> dport = 7777` (killing just that connection) made the AMF open a new connection
  immediately, the SMF answered again, and UE PDU sessions completed within ~1 s — i.e. the client
  *can* recover, it just never decides to.

Suggested fix (patch ready for `lib/sbi/client.c` / `lib/sbi/client.h`):

- count **consecutive** timeouts per SBI client (reset on any successful response),
- after ≥3 consecutive timeouts with a minimum 5 s interval between resets, tear the connection
  pool down by recreating the `CURLM` handle (that is the only way to make libcurl forget and
  close cached connections), failing the in-flight requests explicitly so upper layers get a
  result instead of hanging.

With the patch, the same run reports **0** timeouts after the overload and full service recovery
without restarting any process (A/B: 23 815 → 59 → 0 across successive iterations).

We are happy to iterate on this in a PR — the patch is self-contained (≈60 lines, no API
change, no behaviour change while the peer is healthy).
